business_process: Cold storage, refrigeration, and cold-chain monitoring
description: Ammonia refrigeration of coolers, the freezer warehouse, and loaded trailers; temperature monitoring and alerting for the cold storage CCPs
process_owner: Director of Supply Chain and Logistics
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cold storage is a CCP for refrigerated products and must be monitored at the frequency in the HACCP plan (9 CFR 417.2(c)(4)); more than 2 hours without monitoring leaves a CCP record gap and forces evaluation of every affected lot (417.3(b)); about $9 million of product is on hand
manual_workaround: Refrigeration keeps running on its local controller if SCADA is lost; hourly manual thermometer log by warehouse staff (written Plant 1 procedure); move product to trailers on shore power
dependent_third_parties: Cold-chain monitoring vendor; Plant 1 refrigeration contractor; electric utility; generator fuel supplier
dependent_people_or_facilities: Refrigeration technicians; warehouse staff; Plant 1 engine room, coolers, and freezer warehouse
quantified_operational_impact: About 180 sensors; the manual log needs 3 staff per shift; product holds start after 2 hours without records
quantified_regulatory_impact: CCP record gap; documented 417.3(b) review for each affected lot; FSIS inspection personnel informed
food_and_worker_safety_impact: Severe: temperature abuse can allow pathogen growth in ready-to-eat products

description: Smokehouse and spiral oven cook cycles and chill tunnels for bacon, franks, smoked sausage, hams, and deli logs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Product in a cycle when control or recording is lost must be held and evaluated (9 CFR 417.3(b)); lethality and stabilization records are needed before release (417.5(c)); about 60% of Plant 1 revenue is cooked product
manual_workaround: Smokehouse and oven controllers run stored cycles locally; chart recorders on 4 of 8 smokehouses; manual probe readings every 30 minutes; finish or abort cycles and hold the product
quantified_operational_impact: 8 smokehouses and 2 spiral ovens; about 520,000 lb of cooked product a day; 8 hours down loses about one shift
quantified_regulatory_impact: Missing lethality or stabilization records make product unreleasable; records not maintained can support a finding that the HACCP system is inadequate (417.6(d))
food_and_worker_safety_impact: Severe: undercooking or slow chilling (Listeria monocytogenes, Clostridium perfringens)

business_process: Formulation, cure and brine dosing, and injection
description: Formulation release in the MES; automated brine and cure (sodium nitrite) dosing to 2 brine injectors; CIP of the brine systems
process_owner: Vice President of Food Safety and Quality Assurance
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cured and injected products cannot run without verified formulations; a wrong nitrite level is a chemical hazard; formulations change rarely, so the last approved release is an acceptable recovery point, but restored formulations must be verified against the signed master before use
manual_workaround: Hand-weighed cure batches from printed, FSQA-signed formulation sheets with a second-person check; injectors run at fixed rates verified by pickup weights
quantified_operational_impact: About 140 active formulations; hand batching runs at about half the normal rate
quantified_regulatory_impact: Formulation and batching records are needed to release cured product

business_process: Slicing, packaging, foreign material inspection, lot coding, and labeling
description: Slicing lines, packaging, x-ray and metal detection (foreign material CCP), checkweighing, AI vision inspection (AI-001) on Lines 5-7, and lot codes and labels from the MES
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Every Plant 1 product passes packaging, so this is where daily revenue is earned (about $1.32 million per production day); lines stop without MES label and lot data; a wrong label (undeclared allergen, wrong date) is misbranding that can trigger the 24-hour FSIS notice (9 CFR 418.2); slicing is the post-lethality exposure step for deli meats (9 CFR 430.4)
manual_workaround: Pre-printed label stock with manual lot codes and a second-person check; x-ray units and metal detectors run standalone; AI-001 switched to bypass
dependent_third_parties: Label stock supplier; AI vision inspection vendor
quantified_operational_impact: 9 packaging lines; 12 hours down is about three quarters of a production day (about $990,000 of output), of which about 30% is not recovered
quantified_regulatory_impact: Misbranding exposure if manual labels are wrong
food_and_worker_safety_impact: Moderate: foreign material or allergen mislabeling if workarounds fail

business_process: Sanitation, CIP, and Listeria environmental monitoring
description: Third-shift sanitation, CIP of brine and injector systems, pre-operational inspection, food contact surface testing, and hold-and-test decisions
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Production cannot start without pre-operational sanitation and its records (9 CFR 416.13, 416.16); food contact surface results drive hold-and-test decisions under Alternative 2 (430.4(b)(2)); one missed sanitation window delays the next production day
manual_workaround: Paper Sanitation SOP and pre-operational records; CIP in manual mode with sanitation supervisor sign-off; contract laboratory results by phone and email
quantified_operational_impact: 45 sanitation workers a night; manual CIP takes about 40% longer
quantified_regulatory_impact: Daily Sanitation SOP records with initials and date (416.16(a)); Listeria verification results available to FSIS on request (430.4(c)(7))
food_and_worker_safety_impact: Severe: Listeria monocytogenes on food contact surfaces for ready-to-eat products

business_process: Cold storage, refrigeration, and cold-chain monitoring
description: Ammonia refrigeration of coolers and loaded trailers; temperature monitoring and alerting for the cold storage CCPs
process_owner: Director of Supply Chain and Logistics
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Raw ground and case-ready products are highly perishable; about $3 million of product is on hand; cold storage CCP monitoring (417.2(c)(4)) and 417.3(b) evaluation after a gap
manual_workaround: Refrigeration keeps running on its local controller; move product to trailers on shore power. No written manual temperature log procedure at Plant 2 (gap 9)
dependent_third_parties: Cold-chain monitoring vendor; Plant 2 refrigeration contractor; electric utility
dependent_people_or_facilities: Plant 2 refrigeration technicians; warehouse staff; Plant 2 engine room and coolers
quantified_operational_impact: About 60 sensors; alerts go by SMS to one on-call supervisor
quantified_regulatory_impact: CCP record gap; documented 417.3(b) review for each affected lot
food_and_worker_safety_impact: Severe: pathogen growth in temperature-abused raw ground product

description: Grinders and blenders with inline fat analyzers hit lean-to-fat targets from blend recipes stored in the blender HMIs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Ground product is about 55% of Plant 2 sales; blend targets drive lean-percentage label claims; blend recipes exist only in the HMIs
manual_workaround: Manual blend calculation from batch weights with a laboratory fat test on every batch; QA verifies label claims before release
dependent_third_parties: Plant 2 controls integrator; fat analyzer vendor
quantified_operational_impact: About 240,000 lb of ground product a day; manual blending runs at about 60% of normal rate
quantified_regulatory_impact: Misbranding exposure if lean claims are wrong

business_process: Case-ready cutting, tray packaging, metal detection, and labeling
description: Case-ready cutting lines, modified-atmosphere tray packaging, metal detection, and labels and lot codes from the Plant 2 label server
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Grocery chain delivery windows; every Plant 2 product passes packaging (about $600,000 per production day); the label server sits on the flat network
manual_workaround: Pre-printed labels with manual lot codes and a second-person check; metal detectors run standalone
quantified_operational_impact: About 90,000 trays a day; 12 hours down is about three quarters of a production day, about 30% of it not recovered
quantified_regulatory_impact: Misbranding exposure if manual labels are wrong
food_and_worker_safety_impact: Moderate: foreign material or mislabeling if workarounds fail

business_process: Food safety records and pre-shipment review
description: Electronic HACCP, Sanitation SOP, Listeria, and food defense monitoring records; pre-shipment record review; records for FSIS review
process_owner: Vice President of Food Safety and Quality Assurance
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Product may not ship until its records show every critical limit was met (9 CFR 417.5(c)); records must be available for official review (417.5(f); 416.16(c)); records kept off site must be retrievable within 24 hours of an FSIS request (417.5(e)(2))
manual_workaround: Paper CCP and Sanitation SOP forms; paper pre-shipment review; finished product held in coolers
dependent_people_or_facilities: QA technicians; Plant 1 and Plant 2 FSQA Managers
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,400 CCP and sanitation records a day across both plants
quantified_regulatory_impact: Records not maintained can support a finding that the HACCP system is inadequate (417.6(d))
food_and_worker_safety_impact: Moderate: product cannot ship; no direct hazard while held

business_process: Order management, EDI, warehouse, and shipping
description: Order intake by EDI, release, picking, trailer loading, bills of lading, and advance ship notices for both plants
process_owner: Director of Supply Chain and Logistics
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Grocery chain delivery windows and fill-rate penalties; about 1,900 EDI orders and ship notices a week
manual_workaround: Paper pick lists from the last order export; customer orders by email and phone; handwritten bills of lading
dependent_third_parties: ERP vendor; WMS vendor; EDI network provider; carriers
dependent_people_or_facilities: Warehouse and shipping staff; customer service
quantified_operational_impact: About 80 outbound trailers a day across both plants

business_process: Traceability, recall, and customer traceability portal
description: Lot tracing forward and back; recall execution under 9 CFR 418.3; customer lot lookups, certificates of analysis, and recall notices through the portal
process_owner: Vice President of Food Safety and Quality Assurance
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The 24-hour FSIS notice (9 CFR 418.2) must state the type, amount, origin, and destination of the product, which needs lot tracing; during an active recall the MTD drops to 4 hours; 38 customer organizations use the portal
manual_workaround: Daily traceability export to a controlled offline copy; ERP shipment history; phone and email notices to customers
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider; ERP vendor; WMS vendor
quantified_regulatory_impact: 418.2 notice content; customer recall effectiveness checks
food_and_worker_safety_impact: Severe during a recall (affected product stays in commerce longer)

business_process: Receiving of carcasses, primals, trim, and ingredients
description: Receiving inspection, temperature checks, supplier lot capture, putaway
process_owner: Director of Supply Chain and Logistics
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Perishable inbound loads must be checked and refrigerated on arrival; suppliers can hold loads about a day; supplier lot data feed traceability
manual_workaround: Paper receiving log with handheld thermometers; supplier lot numbers keyed later
quantified_regulatory_impact: Incoming lot records feed recall tracing
food_and_worker_safety_impact: Moderate: temperature-abused raw materials accepted by mistake

business_process: Ammonia refrigeration process safety monitoring and emergency response
description: Ammonia detection, alarms, interlocks, emergency shutdown, and supervision of the refrigeration controllers under the PSM and RMP programs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Loss of supervisory control or alarm visibility over about 60,000 lb of anhydrous ammonia is a worker and community safety issue; controls, alarms, and interlocks are PSM mechanical integrity equipment (29 CFR 1910.119(j)(1)(v); 40 CFR 68.73(a)(5))
manual_workaround: Hardwired ammonia detectors and local alarms work without the controller network; engine rooms are staffed around the clock; compressors switched to manual operation under the PSM operating procedures
quantified_operational_impact: 2 engine rooms; about 60,000 lb of anhydrous ammonia in total
quantified_regulatory_impact: PSM and RMP incident investigation within 48 hours of an incident that could reasonably have resulted in a catastrophic release (1910.119(m)(2); 68.81(b)); CERCLA and EPCRA release reports if 100 lb or more is released in 24 hours (40 CFR 302.4, 302.6)
food_and_worker_safety_impact: Severe: toxic release affecting workers and neighbors

business_process: Production planning, scheduling, and demand forecasting
description: Weekly production plans, line schedules, and raw material requirements; ERP demand forecasting (AI-002)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Plants can run 2 days from the last published plan; forecasts feed raw material purchasing
manual_workaround: Run the last published plan; planners work from spreadsheet exports

description: Raw material, ingredient, and packaging purchase orders; supplier approvals
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Purchase orders are placed days ahead; suppliers accept phone and email orders under standing contracts
manual_workaround: Phone and email orders against standing contracts

business_process: Finance, accounts receivable, and customer billing
description: EDI invoicing, cash application, collections, and lender reporting
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $9.2 million of invoices a week; collections are delayed, not lost
manual_workaround: Invoice the largest customers manually; draw on the revolving credit line
quantified_operational_impact: About $9.2 million of invoices a week; about $3.9 million of cash is delayed at the 72-hour MTD (delayed, not lost)

business_process: Payroll, HR, timekeeping, and staffing agencies
description: Weekly payroll for hourly employees, time capture, onboarding and terminations, agency temporary time records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Weekly payroll for about 760 hourly employees; missed pay drives absenteeism at the plants; wage payment obligations
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll provider; paper time sheets; agencies bill from their own records
quantified_operational_impact: About 850 employees and up to 120 agency temporaries

business_process: Customer service, complaints, and regulatory communications
description: Customer complaints (which may signal adulteration), customer notices, and coordination with FSIS inspection personnel
process_owner: Vice President of Sales and Customer Service
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A complaint can start the 24-hour FSIS clock (418.2); customer contracts require notice within 24 hours of events affecting safety or committed volumes
manual_workaround: Phone tree on personal mobile phones; complaints logged on paper and phoned to FSQA
quantified_regulatory_impact: 418.2 clock may start from a complaint
food_and_worker_safety_impact: Moderate: slow response to a safety complaint
